title: "Page: Emit A Snakemake Download Workflow"
subtitle: "Use quarto-emit to materialize pipeline files without replacing Snakemake"
format: html

  eval: false
---

This page bridges the single-job download definition and the full aggregation
step. The operator decides which jobs belong in the run; `quarto-emit` and
Snakemake materialize and execute the mechanical workflow.

::: {.manual-prereq title="Confirm The Download Contract Exists"}

Before emitting a Snakemake workflow, confirm that the manual has already
defined:

- the request-grid logic from the orchestration page;
- the single-job parameter contract from the download page;
- the expected output naming pattern for raw ERA5 files.

```{python}
#| eval: false
required_concepts = [
    "request_dicts",
    "download_era5(request_dict, ...)",
    "data/raw/era5land/<country>_<dataset>_<variable>_<year>-<month>.grib",
]
required_concepts
```

:::

::: {.manual-procedure .emit-config-yaml file="workflow/downloads.yaml" title="Emit A Download Configuration File"}

Emit a configuration file recording the download jobs selected for this run.

```yaml
downloads:
  - country: MDG
    dataset: reanalysis-era5-land
    variable: 2m_temperature
    year: 2021
    month: "01"
  - country: NPL
    dataset: reanalysis-era5-land
    variable: total_precipitation
    year: 2021
    month: "01"
```

The file materializes the operator's job-selection decision; it does not make
that decision implicitly.

:::

::: {.manual-procedure .emit-source-py file="workflow/Snakefile" title="Emit A Minimal Snakefile"}

Emit a `Snakefile` that maps each configured job to the Python download function
from the previous page. Snakemake absorbs the repeated mechanical scheduling
steps.

```{python}
# Pseudocode adapted for a Quarto Manual example
configfile: "workflow/downloads.yaml"

DOWNLOADS = config["downloads"]

rule all:
    input:
        expand(
            "data/raw/era5land/{country}_{dataset}_{variable}_{year}-{month}.grib",
            zip,
            country=[job["country"] for job in DOWNLOADS],
            dataset=[job["dataset"] for job in DOWNLOADS],
            variable=[job["variable"] for job in DOWNLOADS],
            year=[job["year"] for job in DOWNLOADS],
            month=[job["month"] for job in DOWNLOADS],
        )

rule download_era5:
    output:
        "data/raw/era5land/{country}_{dataset}_{variable}_{year}-{month}.grib"
    params:
        dataset=lambda wc: wc.dataset,
        variable=lambda wc: wc.variable,
        year=lambda wc: wc.year,
        month=lambda wc: wc.month,
    shell:
        # In a real project this would call the emitted Python download job.
        "python scripts/download_era5.py --country {wildcards.country} "
        "--dataset {params.dataset} --variable {params.variable} "
        "--year {params.year} --month {params.month}"
```

:::

::: {.manual-check title="Check The Snakemake Integration Contract"}

Verify that the emitted files exist and that Snakemake accepts the workflow in
dry-run mode.

```{python}
#| eval: false
assert Path("workflow/downloads.yaml").exists()
assert Path("workflow/Snakefile").exists()
```

```{python}
import subprocess
result = subprocess.run(["snakemake", "--dry-run"], capture_output=True, text=True)
assert result.returncode == 0, f"Snakemake dry-run failed: {result.stderr}"
```

:::
